title: Polymorphism and Abstraction
relevance: Interviewers use duck typing, dunder methods, and ABCs to check whether candidates can customize shared interfaces and choose flexible vs strict contracts in Python.

phases.goal: Establish what polymorphism and abstraction mean and how duck typing differs from inheritance-style sharing.

must_hit.point: Polymorphism means many forms: different types can respond to the same method call in their own specific way.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says objects of different types share a method name but each type supplies its own behavior.

must_hit.point: If inheritance is about sharing behavior, polymorphism is about customizing behavior under a shared name.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Contrasts shared inherited behavior with customized behavior behind one method name.

must_hit.point: Abstraction hides complex implementation details behind a simple interface; an ABC is a blueprint that cannot be instantiated and forces subclasses to implement specific methods.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Defines abstraction as a simple interface over hidden details and ABC as a non-instantiable blueprint with required methods.

probes: What does polymorphism mean in programming, and how does it differ from inheritance?

hints.1: Think about the phrase many forms and a shared method name.
hints.2: Contrast sharing behavior through inheritance with customizing behavior under one name.
hints.3: Polymorphism: different types respond to the same call their own way; inheritance shares, polymorphism customizes under a shared name.

phases.goal: Show how duck typing, dunder/operator overloading, and ABCs actually work in Python.

must_hit.point: In duck typing, Python does not require the object to be an instance of a specific base class; it only checks that the needed method exists at call time.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says animal_sound works on Dog/Cat/Robot because each has speak(), not because of a shared Animal parent.

must_hit.point: Magic/dunder methods let you define how operators and built-ins like +, ==, and str() behave on custom objects.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions __add__/__str__/__eq__ and that p1 + p2 calls __add__.

must_hit.point: An ABC is created by inheriting from ABC and marking required methods with @abstractmethod from the abc module.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes from abc import ABC, abstractmethod, subclassing ABC, and decorating required methods.

probes: How does duck typing decide whether animal_sound(entity) is valid, and how would you overload + for a Point class?

hints.1: Ask what Python looks for on the object at the moment speak() is called.
hints.2: Separate runtime method presence from class hierarchy, then name the dunder for +.
hints.3: Duck typing only needs speak() present; Point.__add__ defines +, and ABCs use ABC plus @abstractmethod.

phases.goal: Choose when flexible duck typing is enough versus when a strict ABC contract is warranted.

must_hit.point: Duck typing enables loosely coupled, swappable components as long as they implement the expected interface.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says systems stay flexible because callers depend on behavior (e.g. speak), not on a fixed type.

must_hit.point: Duck typing assumes consenting adults and trust; ABCs enforce contracts strictly so required methods exist before the program relies on them.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Prefers duck typing for small/trusted code and ABCs when a large system needs a guaranteed method like process_payment().

probes: When would you prefer duck typing over an Abstract Base Class, and when would you flip that choice?

hints.1: Compare trust-based flexibility with compile-or-instantiate-time enforcement.
hints.2: Map duck typing to swappable interfaces and ABCs to guaranteed methods in larger systems.
hints.3: Duck typing for loosely coupled trusted code; ABCs when every PaymentProcessor must implement process_payment before use.

phases.goal: Apply polymorphism via duck typing, dunders, or ABCs to a concrete design or coding task.

must_hit.point: A function can accept any object with the expected method (e.g. speak) without requiring a shared parent class.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Walks through animal_sound calling entity.speak() on Dog, Cat, and Robot interchangeably.

must_hit.point: Subclassing an ABC without implementing its abstract methods fails when you try to instantiate the concrete class; the ABC itself also cannot be instantiated.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says forgetting process_payment crashes on instantiate, and PaymentProcessor() raises TypeError.

must_hit.point: Operator behavior for a custom type is implemented by writing the matching dunder, such as __add__ for + or __eq__ for equality.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Points to Vector/Point __add__ and filling in __eq__ to compare the .x fields.

probes: How would you enforce that every PaymentProcessor implements process_payment, and how would you make two Vector objects comparable with ==?

hints.1: Think contract enforcement with abc, and equality via a dunder.
hints.2: ABC + @abstractmethod for the payment API; __eq__ comparing vector components.
hints.3: Inherit PaymentProcessor(ABC), implement process_payment; for Vector, def __eq__(self, other): return self.x == other.x.

tradeoffs.topic: Duck typing vs Abstract Base Classes
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Duck typing is flexible and loosely coupled: callers trust that objects quack (have the method) and components can be swapped without a shared base type, but missing methods surface as AttributeError at runtime. ABCs trade that flexibility for a strict contract—using ABC and @abstractmethod so subclasses must implement required methods and the abstract class itself cannot be instantiated—better when a large system needs guaranteed interfaces like process_payment().

gotchas.trap: Assuming duck typing will fail early or type-check that an object is an Animal before calling speak().
gotchas.correction: Python only checks for the method at call time; a missing speak() raises AttributeError at runtime and can crash the program.

gotchas.trap: Trying to instantiate an ABC directly, or instantiating a subclass that omitted an @abstractmethod.
gotchas.correction: ABCs cannot be instantiated (TypeError), and a concrete subclass must implement every abstract method or instantiation fails.
